findings.violating_statement: The section does not provide the manufacturer's name as required; it only lists address details without stating the legal name of the manufacturer.
findings.source_quote: Table 2: Manufacturer’s Details Name Address: Phone; Survey No.: 48/3 & 48/7, Pashan Sus Road, Sus Village, Taluka Mulshi, Pune-411021 Maharashtra, INDIA.
findings.explanation: Annex XII.2#1 mandates that the CER include the name and address of the manufacturer. The provided text lists address information but omits the manufacturer's legal name, breaching this requirement.
findings.suggested_correction: Insert the manufacturer's legal name before the address, e.g., "Manufacturer Name: BioRad Medisys Ltd; Address: Survey No.: 48/3 & 48/7, Pashan Sus Road, ..."

findings.violating_statement: The administrative particulars provide only the Basic UDI‑DI codes for the devices and do not include the required UDI‑PI information such as the serial or lot number for these implantable devices.
findings.source_quote: Basic UDI-DI Codes: Double J Stent & Kit Blue (Short Term); 890551639TL. Basic UDI-DI Codes: Blue HC; 8905516101AW. Basic UDI-DI Codes: Blue Set; 890551640T5.
findings.explanation: Annex VI C.6.b mandates that for implantable devices the serial number or lot number (UDI‑PI) must be identified. The CER section lists only the UDI‑DI values and omits any UDI‑PI data, which is a non‑compliance with the MDR requirement.
findings.suggested_correction: Include the UDI‑PI (e.g., lot or serial number) for each listed implantable device alongside the Basic UDI‑DI, for example: "Basic UDI‑DI: 890551639TL; UDI‑PI (lot): L12345".

findings.violating_statement: The description lacks required safety information, warnings, precautions and contraindications as required by Annex I.23.s#1
findings.source_quote: Double J Stent is used for treatment of the upper urinary tract are implantable devices that support the flow of the urine from the kidneys to the bladder.
findings.explanation: Annex I.23.s#1 mandates that the device information includes warnings, precautions, contraindications and limitations of use. The section provides only a functional description and does not contain any such safety information.
findings.suggested_correction: Include a safety information paragraph, e.g., "Warnings: Do not use in patients with known allergy to PTFE or hydrophilic coatings. Contraindications: Active urinary tract infection, severe ureteral obstruction. Precautions: Ensure correct placement to avoid migration; monitor for hematuria or pain post‑implantation."

raw.source_quote: It is supplied as sterile/nonsterile product in a peel-open package and intended for one time use only.

raw.violating_statement: The section states the device is sterilized by EtO but provides no evidence that the sterilisation method has been validated as required by Annex I.11.d
raw.source_quote: Sterilization Method; Specifications: Ethylene Oxide (EtO) sterilized.
raw.explanation: Annex I.11.d mandates that devices labelled as sterile shall be processed, manufactured, packaged and sterilised by means of appropriate, validated methods. The CER only mentions the method without confirming validation, thus the requirement is not satisfied.

findings.violating_statement: The report does not provide any statement confirming the compatibility between the different parts of the device, which is required by Annex I > (10) > (c).
findings.source_quote: The materials selected for device construction are widely used in urological medical devices and are suitable for short-term internal use.
findings.explanation: Annex I.10.c mandates that the compatibility between the different parts of a device consisting of more than one implantable part be demonstrated. The section only describes individual materials without any assessment of their mutual compatibility (e.g., chemical interaction, mechanical integration).
findings.suggested_correction: Add a statement such as: "Compatibility testing between the polyurethane stent, polypropylene accessories, and the stainless steel/Nitinol guidewire has been performed in accordance with ISO 10993-5 and ISO 10993-12, confirming no adverse chemical or mechanical interactions under intended use conditions."

findings.violating_statement: The report lacks confirmation that the device meets defined chemical and/or physical specifications as required by Annex I > (10) > (h).
findings.source_quote: The materials selected for device construction are widely used in urological medical devices and are suitable for short-term internal use.
findings.explanation: Annex I.10.h requires documentation that the device meets defined chemical and physical specifications and that risks from contaminants or residues are minimized. The section does not provide any such specifications or verification data.
findings.suggested_correction: Include a statement such as: "All materials comply with the applicable chemical and physical specifications (e.g., ISO 10993-1, ISO 10993-12) and have been verified for absence of harmful residues after EtO sterilisation."

raw.source_quote: The mechanism of action is mechanical and is based on the following: 1. Internal Urinary Drainage ...
raw.explanation: Annex.II.1.d mandates that the principles of operation and mode of action be scientifically demonstrated if necessary, but the text only describes the mechanism without any supporting scientific data or references.
raw.suggested_correction: Include a summary of scientific studies or data that demonstrate the mechanical principle of action, such as bench testing results, fluid dynamics analyses, or clinical evidence supporting the described drainage mechanism.

findings.violating_statement: The section does not indicate the sterilisation method for the sterile device, which is required by Annex I.23.l
findings.source_quote: This is a single use sterile device which is used for internal drainage from Kidney to Bladder in medical conditions like improper urine drainage, calculi in ureter, hydronephrosis, oxalate calculi, pyeloplasty with UPJ Obstruction, residual renal calculus, ureteral stricture.
findings.explanation: Annex I.23.l mandates that if a device is supplied sterile, the CER must include an indication of its sterile state and the sterilisation method. While the text states the device is sterile, it does not specify the sterilisation method, making the requirement unmet.
findings.suggested_correction: Add a statement such as: "The device is supplied sterile, having been sterilised by ethylene oxide (EO) according to validated sterilisation process XYZ, with accompanying bioburden and sterility assurance level data."

findings.violating_statement: The sterilisation method is not indicated despite the device being supplied sterile
findings.source_quote: This is a single use sterile device used for internal drainage from Kidney to Bladder
findings.explanation: Annex I.23.l requires that if the device is supplied sterile, the CER must indicate its sterile state and the sterilisation method. The text only states the device is sterile but does not specify the method used.
findings.suggested_correction: This is a single‑use sterile device, sterilised by ethylene oxide, used for internal drainage from kidney to bladder

findings.violating_statement: No information is provided on characteristics that could pose a risk if the single‑use device were re‑used
findings.source_quote: This is a single use sterile device used for internal drainage from Kidney to Bladder
findings.explanation: Because the device is indicated for single use, Annex I.23.p#1 requires information on known characteristics and technical factors that could pose a risk if the device were re‑used. The section contains no such information.
findings.suggested_correction: If re‑used, the device may retain residual sterilant and structural degradation that could lead to infection or failure; therefore it must not be re‑used. Detailed risk information is available in the manufacturer’s risk management file upon request.

raw.violating_statement: The section does not provide patient selection criteria, contraindications or warnings as required for the intended patient population description
raw.source_quote: Double J Stent (Short term) is manufactured to meet requirements of medical conditions like Improper urine drainage, calculi in ureter, hydronephrosis, oxalate calculi, pyeloplasty with UPJ Obstruction, residual renal calculus, ureteral stricture. These medical conditions commonly occur in adult Male, Female during urological procedures. Hence Double J Stent (Short term) can be use in Adults, Male / Female.
raw.explanation: Annex II.1.c mandates that the intended patient population description include patient selection criteria, indications, contra‑indications and warnings. The provided text only lists medical conditions and a broad adult population, omitting any contraindications, selection criteria or warnings, thus non‑compliant.
raw.suggested_correction: Include a subsection that specifies patient selection criteria, explicit contraindications (e.g., known hypersensitivity to device materials, active urinary infection), and relevant warnings/precautions for the Double J Stent (Short term).

findings.violating_statement: The statement that no clinical investigation was performed is not justified under Article 61(4) which requires a clinical investigation for implantable devices unless specific exemption criteria are met, which are not demonstrated in the text.
findings.source_quote: Hence, according to MDR article 61, no clinical investigation was performed.
findings.explanation: Article 61(4) mandates clinical investigations for implantable devices unless the device is a modified version of a marketed device with demonstrated equivalence and notified body endorsement. The CER section provides no evidence of such an exemption, making the claim non‑compliant.
findings.suggested_correction: Provide evidence that the device meets an exemption under Art.61.4 (e.g., it is a modification of a marketed device with demonstrated equivalence and notified‑body endorsement) or conduct and document a clinical investigation as required.

findings.violating_statement: The section does not describe a post‑market surveillance plan covering the required elements (methods for data collection, assessment, indicators, trend analysis, communication procedures, corrective actions, traceability and PMCF justification) as required by Annex III.b.
findings.source_quote: The device is marketed in India. The following data sources were utilised to collect relevant post‑marketing data to support clinical safety and performance.
findings.explanation: Annex III.b mandates that the PMS plan shall include a proactive systematic process, effective assessment methods, suitable indicators, trend analysis procedures, communication methods, corrective action procedures, traceability tools and a PMCF plan or justification. The provided section only lists data sources and distribution/complaint data without describing any of these required plan components, thus non‑compliant.
findings.suggested_correction: Add a dedicated subsection describing the post‑market surveillance plan that outlines: (i) systematic data collection processes and comparison with similar products, (ii) methods and tools for data assessment, (iii) defined indicators and thresholds for benefit‑risk reassessment, (iv) procedures for trend analysis and statistical significance testing, (v) communication protocols with authorities and users, (vi) procedures for initiating corrective actions and traceability, and (vii) the PMCF plan or justification for its non‑applicability.
